title: introduce-lookahead-prefetch-and-decode-synchronizer-with-gradient-aware-kvcache
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Added lookahead prefetch scheduler and decode synchronizer that reduces tail latency for interactive loads; no API changes. Includes perf tests and docs.
description: Summary: Implement a lookahead prefetch stage and a decode synchronizer that uses lightweight sampling (opportunistic sketching) to predict near-future KV cache accesses and inform speculative prefetch depth. This change targets interactive/low-latency workloads where small sequence bursts cause repeated KV misses and decode stalls. The new path keeps prefill and decode stages decoupled but tightly coordinated to increase overlap while bounding extra compute and memory.
body: Context and motivation: On interactive workloads we observed recurring stalls at the start of decode when KV cache misses were frequent for short, high-cardinality prefixes. Prior work improved packing and chunking, but we still see oscillation between aggressive prefetching (wasting GPU cycles and memory) and conservative behavior (higher P99 latency). This PR introduces a lightweight lookahead prefetch scheduler that: 1) collects small, rolling token-access sketches per-request to estimate near-term KV locality; 2) computes a bounded prefetch depth per-request based on estimated benefit vs. expected cost (GPU cycles + KV memory pressure); 3) signals the decode stage with a synchronization token so decode can proceed opportunistically once critical prefixes are available.
body_continued: What changed (high level): - runtime/scheduler/lookahead_prefetch.py: new scheduler that runs inside the serving runtime and exposes a compact policy API. Uses streaming reservoir sampling over recent token indices and a tiny locality score. - runtime/kernel/kv_cache_manager.cc: added prefetch primitives and a soft-reservation mechanism so lookahead prefetch can tentatively allocate KV slots without evicting hot entries. - runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.rs: updated admission path to accept prefetch hints and to fold prefetch work into existing micro-batch windows (no extra global scheduling thread). - runtime/decode/synchronizer.cc: small handshake token and fast-path unlock so decode can proceed once lookahead signals the minimum KV prefix ready. - tests/perf/test_lookahead_prefetch.py: microbench harness reproducing short-interaction tail cases; includes comparison against baseline (no-lookahead) and speculative-full-prefetch. - docs/notes/lookahead-prefetch.md: design rationale and tuning knobs (crediting threshold, max-prefetch-depth, sketch window). - examples/benchmarks/ci_prefetch_profile.yaml: CI perf job to run the new microbench.
commits_summary: 5 commits: (1) initial lookahead scheduler prototype and tests, (2) KV prefetch API and soft-reservation, (3) batcher integration and handshake token, (4) perf harness and CI job, (5) follow-up tuning and unit test fixes.
testing_and_ci: CI initially failed on a flaky perf assertion in test_lookahead_prefetch (time-bound). Fixed by switching from wall-clock to token-count based assertions and adding a small headroom constant. Full test matrix: unit (pass), integration (pass), perf (baseline comparison run in CI job passed within thresholds). Linting: pass. Pre-merge benchmarking: 12% P95 reduction and 18% P99 reduction on the short-interaction synthetic suite used in ENG-2109.
review_conversation: - Ethan: asked for a safety cap to avoid unbounded prefetch under adversarial requests; implemented a max_prefetch_depth config and safeguard in kv_cache_manager. - Priya: requested clearer metrics to drive future autotuning; added counters (prefetch_attempts, prefetch_hits, prefetch_evictions) and a dashboard note. - Marco: suggested folding prefetch hints into existing microbatch windows to avoid an extra scheduling thread; updated continuous_batcher integration accordingly. Author replies: addressed each comment, added unit tests for soft-reservation, and documented tuning knobs in docs. Final approval by Ethan and Priya, Marco approved with comment.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-11-02 after re-running CI. No revert required.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overly aggressive prefetch could increase memory pressure and evict hot KV entries. Mitigation: soft-reservation prevents immediate eviction and a conservative default max_prefetch_depth=4; metric alarms added to detect prefetch-driven evictions. Also added feature-flag gating behind runtime config to allow quick rollback per-customer.
performance_notes: Benchmarked on p4d-like instance with standard model set: - Short-interaction synthetic: P95 -12%, P99 -18% - Throughput impact on sustained long-batch workloads: negligible (<1% variance) since prefetch is bounded and folded into micro-batches. - Memory: worst-case additional KV reservations ~3-6% of per-shard KV memory under default settings.
how_to_rollout: 1) feature-flag off by default in hosted; enable for internal perf experiments. 2) Run CI perf job to validate thresholds. 3) Gradual rollout to 5% traffic, monitor prefetch_evictions and latency metrics for 48h. 4) Increase to 25% if stable, then full rollout.
notes_for_backport: Non-breaking; low-risk. If backporting to 2025.10 maintenance branch, include kv_cache_manager soft-reservation changes and the microbatch admission updates. Perf harness can be excluded.
docs: docs/notes/lookahead-prefetch.md describes policy parameters, expected tradeoffs, and recommended tuning for Dedicated and Private deployments.
acknowledgements: Thanks to SRE for perf harness infra and to Research for the lightweight sketch design review.
